note: Eight repo-authored items for the eval-harness stub (gpu.lab.eval). NOT lm-eval, NOT WikiText, NOT MMLU. The 12-item hard plate (hard_items.json) is unchanged and is still the reasoning plate. No item is a HuggingFace row id: every gold is in this file, so nothing here can tempt a download. Task names copy lm-eval spelling so a later real harness can emit the same strings; the prompts are ours.

items.note: repo-authored arithmetic; shares the extract_number scorer with the hard plate
items.prompt: A crate holds 12 jars. A warehouse receives 8 full crates and then 24 loose jars. How many jars does it have in total? Show the steps, then put the final integer after ####.

items.note: fence-post count; the run is 80 m and both ends carry a post
items.prompt: A straight fence run is 80 meters long. One post is placed every 4 meters, and both ends of the run carry a post. How many posts are needed? Show the steps, then put the final integer after ####.

items.note: MMLU-shaped letter extract, fail closed; not an MMLU row
items.prompt:
Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets between separate networks?
A. Data link layer
B. Network layer
C. Transport layer
D. Session layer
Reply with the letter only.

choices: It becomes denser than liquid water
items.note: ARC-shaped; water expands on freezing, so the 'denser' distractor is the myth
items.prompt:
Liquid water freezes into ice at standard pressure. What happens to the water?
A. Its mass increases
B. Its temperature rises
C. Its volume increases
D. It becomes denser than liquid water
Reply with the letter only.

items.note: Winogrande-shaped pronoun binding, asked as a binary so the yesno scorer applies
items.prompt: The trophy did not fit in the suitcase because it was too large. Does "it" refer to the suitcase? Reply with Yes or No only.

items.note: TruthfulQA-shaped: the school answer 'exactly five' is the myth. Neither phrase present is pending_human, never a silent pass.
items.prompt: According to modern physiology, do humans have exactly five senses or more than five? Answer in one short sentence.
